title: Public records checks and outcomes
question: Which suspicions held up when compared with contracts, audit findings, receipts and responses?
finding: 30 focused reviews compare reported figures to their underlying records and identify the documents that could change each conclusion.
how: Reviewers checked the issue against the terms and reporting period in force and compared agency responses, later corrections, receipts and alternative explanations where available.
limits: Raw keyword matches only locate passages. The evidence column records what the original records established. Each linked source is a starting point; case files retain the complete citation set.

rows.subject: Transit cleaning and event funding
rows.scope: Two BART contractor investigations and the America’s Cup host agreement
rows.result: BART confirmed an $11,900 recovery. The event agreement separated a performance bond from fundraising.
rows.gap: The final sweeping settlement amount and ultimate distribution of event back wages remain open.

document.t: Investigation 205-2024, September 3, 2024, findings, evidence tables, contract terms and response

rows.subject: Airport leases and union lobbying
rows.scope: Four airport audits and 1,482 disclosed union-client contacts
rows.result: Three operators had $74,407 in unassessed rent late fees. Two closely matched legislative appeals had different outcomes.
rows.gap: A monthly lobbying payment cannot be allocated to a particular hearing from the filing alone.

document.t: Avis Budget, rent verification, fee calculation and responses, full report in Board file 140895 pp. 41–53

rows.subject: Permit signers and competitive bids
rows.scope: 17 permit applications at 14 parcels and 420 bidder entries on 108 documents
rows.result: Eight losing bidders appeared on seven winning project teams. Six overlaps were disclosed in the original proposals.
rows.gap: Who performed and received payment for each scope requires the project payrolls and vouchers.

document.t: Adopted resolution 2026-0085, corrected October 9, awarding Mission SoMa street improvements to R&S

rows.subject: Fleet auctions and utility suppliers
rows.scope: Fleet disposal accounts and a federal sentencing and garnishment record
rows.result: A supplier admitted about $17,923.50 in bribes to two SFPUC employees. The court ordered $19,762.90 for San Francisco.
rows.gap: The City’s receipts and auction-lot remittances remain unverified.

document.t: Sentencing of Sheldon Morris, San Francisco payments and city-by-city restitution

rows.subject: Power procurement and credit penalties
rows.scope: Five California capacity citations and a separate renewable-credit proceeding
rows.result: The state recorded $3,516,568 received on five citations. A separate $10,010,909 preliminary assessment ended at $500 paid.
rows.gap: The alternative cost of buying capacity requires contemporary procurement offers.

document.t: Energy Citations Issued, June 2024, pages 3–4, five dated CleanPowerSF payments

rows.subject: Library capital and operating transfers
rows.scope: Seven year-end Library Preservation Fund transfers and the capital closeout presentation
rows.result: $24,826,247 matched the General Fund receiving entries. City Charter section 16.109(c) requires returning the uncommitted baseline share.
rows.gap: The year-end controller calculations and a signed capital closeout by source would settle the remaining reconciliation.

document.t: Controller spending and revenue dataset

rows.subject: Ferry scheduling and reimbursements
rows.scope: Regulatory operating conditions and separate WETA cancellation reports
rows.result: The CPUC ordered PropSF to pay $10,000 for operating a published schedule before approval. Its register marks the obligation in compliance.
rows.gap: The register gives no deposit date, and cancellation counts do not identify contractor service credits.

document.t: PropSF stipulation admitting scheduled service, pages 1–4

rows.subject: School bus claims and settlements
rows.scope: Two separate SFUSD court matters and the March 2023 board minutes
rows.result: The board approved $1 million payable to the district on disputed pandemic invoices. The earlier maintenance suit ended in a separate gross settlement.
rows.gap: Neither settlement establishes when the district received the money.

document.t: Official minutes of March 27, 2023, closed-session report p. 1 and adoption p. 2

rows.subject: Streetlight outage response
rows.scope: Repair targets, city performance reports and CPUC Decision 14-08-032
rows.result: City reports document missed repair targets. The state adopted performance goals and deferred a proposed bill credit.
rows.gap: No later order or invoice reviewed established a credit payable for a particular outage.

document.t: CPUC Decision 14-08-032, pp. 182–185

rows.subject: Animal shelter capital closeout
rows.scope: Shelter capital reporting, construction acceptance and bid history
rows.result: Public Works reported finishing $7.9 million below budget. Project reporting placed substantial completion in the planned winter window.
rows.gap: No improper contingency payment or collectible contractor credit was established.

document.t: Public Works closeout presentation, slide 11

rows.subject: Food assistance errors and recoveries
rows.scope: Seven years of state wage-match reports and city account 479997
rows.result: In FY2026 the state established $1,642,414 in overissuances, including $338,478 in administrative errors. The City booked $396,103.93 net collections.
rows.gap: The state and City figures have different claim populations. Signed quarterly reports and reconciliations are needed.

document.t: DSS 466 Fraud Investigation Activity Report, by county and quarter (latest workbook; earlier years in the same series)

rows.subject: Arts grants and sponsor accounts
rows.scope: Historical Controller audits and recommendation tracking
rows.result: Three sponsor-held accounts bypassed City payment rules. The separate SOMArts grant audit identified $339 in charges, with substitute costs proposed.
rows.gap: The sponsor-account payments were unquantified and final settlement of the $339 is unverified.

document.t: Financial Management Review of the San Francisco Arts Commission, pp. 3–4 and D-1

rows.subject: Housing allowances and payment standards
rows.scope: 94 housing authority packets and five annual audits
rows.result: Four late reexaminations occurred in the FY2025 sample of 60. Auditors identified no questioned costs for that finding.
rows.gap: Household-level files and effective schedules are needed to test specific benefit calculations.

document.t: Budget and Legislative Analyst, table 9.2, printed p. 90

rows.subject: Airline fees and refunds
rows.scope: Separate carrier landing-fee and federal overhead audits
rows.result: China Airlines’ passenger fees were $50,594 short after a credit. Separately, SFO documented $4.55 million returned to carrier accounts.
rows.gap: The China Airlines fee receipt and final interest decision remain unverified.

document.t: Report SC-2004-038 on revenue diversions at SFO, tables 1 and 2

rows.subject: Conference lodging charged twice
rows.scope: Seven entries traced across a federal grant and regional college subcontract records
rows.result: Federal auditors retained $8,830 in questioned lodging costs after examining the college’s receipts.
rows.gap: The final federal disposition and any repayment remain unverified.

document.t: Final audit OIG 02-1024, award DUE-9850325, Schedule B note B-3, printed pages 20–23 and Appendix A

rows.subject: Fare collection and system outages
rows.scope: July 2025 Clipper failure, operator claims, board funding and historic cash controls
rows.result: Muni submitted a $62,992 estimate. Regional staff proposed reimbursing that amount and the board approved a regional contingency.
rows.gap: The dated Muni receipt and a recovery from the operator remain unverified.

document.t: Clipper Executive Board, October 20, 2025, item 3b, pages 1–2

rows.subject: Recycled water delivery
rows.scope: Capital reports, budget analyst workpapers and the state water-use table
rows.result: Pre-service pump equipment failure contributed to a $17.03 million project budget increase. Golf course deliveries came from other systems.
rows.gap: Net repair expense and the first metered customer delivery remain unverified.

document.t: April 17, 2024 Budget and Finance Committee report, file 240191, printed pages 8–11

rows.subject: Idle city cellular services
rows.scope: July 2025 departmental inventory and a separate FY2024 FirstNet voucher comparison
rows.result: The budget analyst identified 2,117 idle lines without an approved business use, costing an estimated $82,000 monthly.
rows.gap: The later disconnection dates, actual savings and any specific outage credit remain open.

document.t: Budget and Finance Committee, file 250883, pp. 22–27, especially p. 27

rows.subject: Commissions and vacant leased floors
rows.scope: Floor-specific leases, vouchers and an approved abatement at 1360 Mission
rows.result: Human Services vacated the first two floors. Public Health rented the fourth. A new lease authorized $429,736 in rent abatement.
rows.gap: No dated rent payment for those vacant floors or improper brokerage commission was established.

document.t: HSA authorization

rows.subject: Retiree health trust deposits
rows.scope: Annual contributions and audited trust financial statements for FY2019–FY2026
rows.result: FY2024 and FY2025 statements reported no annual employer contribution deficiency. The FY2026 auditor reported no reportable noncompliance.
rows.gap: Annual statements cannot verify batch-by-batch remittance dates.

document.t: Trust financial report catalog

rows.subject: Dredging quantities and reimbursements
rows.scope: Ten Port vouchers, measurement rules, amended awards and disposal reporting
rows.result: Ten vouchers reconciled to $9,962,625 for contract 2842. The successor’s $9.13 million paid differed from $34.83 million authorized.
rows.gap: Dated surveys, disposal receipts and credits are necessary for an invoice-level quantity test.

document.t: 2022 award

rows.subject: Park concession minimum rents
rows.scope: Two Controller audits, lease clauses, management responses and follow-ups
rows.result: Beach Chalet paid $53,208 in late charges. For Lincoln Park Golf the agency disputed a $124,757 audit calculation under holdover terms.
rows.gap: Closing the recommendations did not document a Lincoln Park collection.

document.t: Lincoln Park Golf Course concession audit, findings 2015-01 and 2015-02 and attached responses

rows.subject: Ethics collections and enforcement deadlines
rows.scope: Signed decisions, settlement votes and delinquent revenue account tables
rows.result: The City settled the disputed Farrell forfeiture for $25,000. In a separate account the Bureau recorded $225 paid and later reported an expired collection window.
rows.gap: Later deposits and formal closing entries require separate collection records.

document.t: May 2017 enforcement report, page 3

rows.subject: Wireless pole license counts
rows.scope: A joint agency briefing, signed wireless resolutions and 1,274 permit records
rows.result: The agency briefing said 578 SFPUC licenses would retain old terms. The adopted resolution used 800 for that same group.
rows.gap: A site-level license ledger with billing dates is needed to verify any unpaid fees.

document.t: Resolution 367-23, pages 2–3 and 5

rows.subject: Storm repairs and insurance proceeds
rows.scope: Maceo May financing, insurance receipts and the May 2023 board follow-up
rows.result: The housing office reported $5.6 million received and $28.6 million expected. The City authorized up to $14.983 million of additional lending.
rows.gap: The closing draw, final insurance settlement and any duplicated recovery remain unverified.

document.t: Maceo May gap loan evaluation, pp. 4–10

rows.subject: Preschool enrollment and attendance
rows.scope: Two consecutive SF State child-development audits and program funding rules
rows.result: Auditors removed 947 eligible enrollment days across six families. The FY2017 audit confirms a $29,156 refund.
rows.gap: The separate attendance correction in another audit had no questioned costs.

document.t: Child Development Fund Report, FY2016, printed pages 22 and 28

rows.subject: Housing cash flow and subordinate loans
rows.scope: 59 passages in 25 files, refinancing records, property accounts and forbearance workouts
rows.result: North Beach’s $2,025,734 FY2025 ground rent reconciles to $800,000 base rent and a $1,225,734 contingent-balance reduction.
rows.gap: Payment ledgers and cash-flow certifications are needed to test balances on the individual loans.

document.t: FY2022 audit, ground lease note

rows.subject: Assessment districts and benefits
rows.scope: 43 passages in 18 files, district annual reports and a district wind-down
rows.result: Fisherman’s Wharf reported $239,950 more assessment revenue than spending in FY2025. A restricted Port grant funded work outside the district.
rows.gap: The revenue difference alone establishes neither an improper charge nor a refund.

document.t: FY2024–25 district annual report, pp. 17, 20

rows.subject: Electric train warranty performance
rows.scope: Caltrain monthly delay reports, support budgets and rolling-stock contracts
rows.result: Caltrain attributed 1,060 delay minutes to Stadler warranty issues in October 2026. The September figure was 392.
rows.gap: The cost of repairs, warranty credits and any liquidated damages remain unverified.

document.t: November 18 advisory staff report, item 11, page 1 (local transcription of October figures)

rows.subject: Permit timing and fees at issuance
rows.scope: Historic building permits, a Board appeal and the City’s payer table
rows.result: The City acknowledged overlooking a $49,712 infrastructure fee on a 2013 permit. All 11 supervisors upheld the assessment in 2023.
rows.gap: The payer table does not identify a subsequent receipt or adjustment.

document.t: Planning response to the Board, case 2010.0681APL, pages 1–2 of memo
